title: INT8 weight-only deployment sanity and regression orchestrator
creator: Marcus Li
description: Create an end-to-end orchestration suite that integrates INT8 weight-only (GPTQ/AWQ) quantization profiles into deployment pipelines and runs regression and chaos scenarios to validate calibration workflows and accuracy stability. This ticket scopes the automation, smoke probes, and Canary gating to ensure rollouts do not regress customer-facing metrics or golden-answer fidelity.
acceptance_criteria: Automated pipeline runs nightly with current INT8 profiles and publishes a regression report to the quant-profiles dashboard
Canary gating prevents promotion if regression delta > 1.5% on golden-answer F1 or > 2% decrease in embedding cosine similarity on benchmark set
Calibration artifacts (scale/zero-point matrices and per-layer bias corrections) are archived with versioned metadata and retrievable by CI ref
Rollback playbook triggers automatically on Canary fail, with a documented 3-step escalation and telemetry snapshot attached
Latency and memory overhead of INT8 variant must be within 10% of baseline non-quantized variant for p95 tail in dedicated pools
technical_notes: Pipeline will reuse existing profile registry API; extend to accept 'profile_origin' tag (gptq|awq|fp8-hybrid)
Introduce shadow-run mode: route 0.5% of production traffic to INT8 variant but do not affect responses; capture prefix KV-cache behavior and token timings
Add golden-answer diff harness that computes token-level edit distance and semantic similarity (embedding-based) per prompt
Telemetry should record per-request profile_id, calibration_version, kernel_selection, hw_backing (A100/V100/RTX) and quantization_backend
Avoid intrusive re-quantization in the hot path; use precomputed weight-only artifacts compatible with runtime kernel expectations
risks: False negatives in golden-answer thresholds due to variance in sampling randomness for stochastic decoders
Hardware-specific kernel mismatches could cause silent accuracy drift on heterogeneous fleets
Large calibration artifact registry could increase storage costs and slow lookups without TTL/compaction
Incorrect rollback automation could flip traffic unexpectedly when multiple rollouts are active
test_plan: Create benchmark corpus of 4k prompts covering instructions, multi-turn chat, code, and multilingual pairs (derived from existing eval suite)
Baseline: run FP32/FP16 model on nightly harness to capture golden answers and token timings
INT8 integration: feed weight-only GPTQ and AWQ profiles through calibration workflow and run E2E inference in a CI sandbox
Chaos scenarios: inject kernel swap, CPU fallback, and simulated KV-cache eviction during canary to verify graceful degradation
Metrics to compute: token-level exact match, normalized BLEU, embedding cosine mean, latency p50/p95, memory delta, and failure rate
Define pass thresholds and automatic failure criteria; publish summary to Slack and the Release channel on failure
rollout_plan: Stage 1 - Nightly validation: run full regression suite in CI and publish report (no traffic)
Stage 2 - Shadow run: enable shadow routing at 0.5% traffic, collect telemetry for 72h
Stage 3 - Canary: route 5% traffic with active responses, monitor golden-answer deltas and latency for 24h
Stage 4 - Gradual ramp: if Canary passes, increment by 10% every 6h until 100% or manual stop
Emergency: automatic rollback on critical thresholds with postmortem scheduling within 48h
